name: Phillips 66
description: Phillips 66 is a downstream energy company that refines crude oil (10 refineries in the US and Europe at 2025-12-31; the Los Angeles refinery stopped fuel production in Q4 2025), markets fuels and lubricants, and runs pipelines and gas processing. Its reported profit in 2025 came mostly from Marketing and Specialties ($4.5B before tax, helped by a $1.9B gain on selling 65% of Germany and Austria retail marketing and a $1B gain on its Coop stake) and from Midstream fees ($2.8B), while Refining lost money ($-274M) despite the biggest revenue. It also owns 50 percent of Chevron Phillips Chemical (CPChem), held as an equity investment so its sales do not appear in consolidated revenue, and makes renewable diesel. It does not produce its own crude oil.

businessLines.name: Midstream
businessLines.how: Charges fees to transport, terminal and store crude and refined products, and to gather, process and fractionate natural gas and NGL, largely under volume-based arrangements; also buys and exports LPG and markets NGL. Much of the work serves Phillips 66 refineries.

businessLines.how: Receives its half of CPChem profits as equity earnings; CPChem makes ethylene, polyethylene, normal alpha olefins, aromatics and styrenics sold worldwide into commodity chemical markets and is building the Golden Triangle Polymers cracker on the US Gulf Coast and a Ras Laffan (Qatar) facility with a co-venturer.

businessLines.name: Refining
businessLines.how: Buys crude and other feedstocks and refines them into gasoline, distillates and aviation fuel sold to its own marketing arm, other marketers and exporters; earns the crack spread, so profit moves with refining margins. 2025 included a $948M impairment of the WRB equity investment (Q3) before Phillips 66 bought the other 50 percent on 2025-10-01 from Cenovus.

businessLines.name: Marketing and Specialties
businessLines.how: Buys refined products (mainly from its own refineries) and resells them wholesale and through branded dealer outlets (Phillips 66, Conoco, 76 in the US; JET in the UK); also makes and sells lubricants and base oils. Earns a per-gallon marketing margin plus product sales; 2025 profit included one-time gains of about $2.9B from asset sales.

businessLines.how: Converts vegetable oils and fats into renewable diesel at the Rodeo Complex and the Humber refinery and sells wholesale, earning credits (RINs, LCFS); 2025 segment lost $380M before tax (2024: -$198M).
